### 1. What the user expresses; simulator behaviour

Opening (sent on turn 1): Denise Ashford, travel manager of Bramlett Hydraulics Co., wants to "upgrade Mara to Premium Economy on her flight home tonight, and you will pay for it on the company card"; "That is the only thing you are calling for." "The company profile is what you speak for." Verification: company phone 7165551934, then billing ZIP 14203. Booking ref DK4TRW, passenger name, agreement number CB18830476 and tour code BH4R2K only if asked. If asked about bags: "Mara told you she checked bags at the counter in Denver". If asked about changes: "the return was moved up to today through your corporate booking tool a week or so ago." She accepts charges that must be posted first as the company's to pay; accepts the quote; runs the purchase when handed over and reports the confirmation. Passive simulator; no procedural hints.

### 4. Scored parameters

Unknowns that the visible surface does not settle (business-product tier terms, no corpus on disk): U1 whether the Business Connect Plus tier waives change fees; U2 its annual spend threshold vs 31,480; U3 whether it lists Crestline Main Cabin among its discount-eligible fare brands; U4 its domestic negotiated discount (short-haul international uses the domestic discount); U5 whether it lists corporate_booking_tool among its eligible booking channels; U6 its corporate checked-bag allowance.

**(A) Change fee for exchange e8b3cd9b** (doc "Change Fee by Journey Origin and Itinerary Class": outside-US origin, short-haul international → Main Cabin "125").
- Fare band rate (doc "Change Fee Fare Bands" + definition "Definition of the Fare That Bands the Change Fee": "Names an active corporate agreement | The fare collected less the ticket's taxes and fees"): 658.36 − 118.36 = 540.00 → **0.96**.
- Notice rate (doc "Notice Rates on Voluntary Change Fees"): 2026-09-15 → 2026-09-24 = 9 days → **0.9**.
- Agreement relief rate (doc "Corporate Agreement Relief on Change Fees"): 0 if U1; else 0.6 if 31,480 ≥ U2; else 1.
- Brand rate (doc "Agreement Brand Rates on Change Fees…"): 0.9 if U3 else 0.97.
- 125 × 0.96 × 0.9 = 108.00 × relief × brand → candidates 0 (waived: nothing owed, nothing recorded) / 58.32 / 62.86 / 97.20 / 104.76. Fall-back (computation doc alone): 125.00.

**(B) Bag charge by count for tag CR1047736** (carries a weight entry and no first/second/third bag charge). Doc "Bag Charge by Place in the Count": direction return (partially flown round trip); place = count charges already in the return direction (1: CR1047735) + 1 = **2**; free allowance = max(brand Main Cabin short-haul international 0, elite: no membership on the ticket, corporate U6); list charge = 0 if 2 ≤ U6, else "a first or second bag on an international itinerary costs the … second-bag fee of its itinerary class" = 65 (short-haul international second bag).
- Fare band rate (doc "Fare Bands for Checked-Bag Charges" + definition "Definition of the Fare That Bands a Checked-Bag Charge": "At least one flown coupon | The fare still unflown"): 658.36 − 329.18 = 329.18 → **0.95**.
- Posting rate (doc "Corporate Posting Rates on Checked-Bag Charges"): active, 3 postings → **0.9**.
- Check-in channel rate (doc "Check-In Channel Rates for Checked Bags"): segment 2 has bag charges paid at the airport → **1.1**.
- 65 × 0.95 × 0.9 × 1.1 = 61.1325 → **61.13** (if U6 < 2; if U6 ≥ 2 → 0.00, still recorded). Position 2. Fall-back: 65.00. Weak evidence on U6: the existing first-bag charges on both directions are 35.00 (not zero), which suggests the corporate allowance did not cover a first bag when they were charged; not a rule, only a record inference.

**(C) Weight-or-size charge for the heaviest bag charged by count on segment 2** = CR1047735 (72 lb vs 56 lb), which carries no weight or size entry. Doc "Weight-or-Size List Charge…" (baseline: weight counted = recorded weight 72 → above 70 → second band 200; size 59 ≤ 62 → 0; fall-back **200.00**).
- Weight counted (doc "How a Checked Bag's Weight Is Counted at Each Check-In Point"): airport → 72 − 3 = **69** → above 50, ≤ 70 → first overweight band fee **100**; size 0 → weight component, `overweight_bag`.
- Weight excess rate (doc "Weight Excess Rates…"): excess 69 − 50 = 19 → "above 5 and at most 20" → **0.8**.
- Fare band rate (doc "Fare Bands for Bag Weight and Size Charges"): fare collected 658.36 → **0.95**.
- Points rate (doc "Corporate Points Rates on Bag Weight and Size Charges"): active, 18,420 ≥ 15,000 → **0.8**.
- Repeat rate (doc "Repeat Rates on Bag Weight and Size Charges"): one weight/size entry already standing (6de602dd) → **1.1**.
- 100 × 0.8 × 0.95 × 0.8 × 1.1 = **66.88**, component overweight_bag.

**(D) Premium Economy upgrade charge, segment 2** (doc "Premium Economy Upgrade Price": Main Cabin "Upgrade into Premium Economy" 99; fall-back **99.00**).
- Travel-day rate: departure today → **0.85**.
- Booking lead rate: issue 2026-09-02 → first flight = flown coupon of segment 1, 2026-09-21 → 19 days → **0.98**.
- Fare band rate (PE): fare collected 658.36 → **0.93**.
- Corporate upgrade rate: active; short-haul international → domestic discount U4: ≥ 10 → 0.8; 1–9 → 0.9; else 1.
- Trip-charge credit (docs "Trip-Charge Credit on Premium Economy Upgrades for Corporate Bookings" + "Measuring a Ticket's Trip Charges"): share 0.1 if U5 else 0; trip charges (one flown coupon) = charges against segment 2 + itinerary-level = 35.00 + 100.00 + (B) + (C) + (A).
- 99 × 0.85 × 0.98 × 0.93 = 76.69431 × corporate rate − share × trip charges, floor 0, round at end.
- Under the record-inferred U6 < 2 and each combination of U1–U5 the charge is one of: 25.33 / 24.58 / 29.22 / 28.77 / 35.05 (rate 0.8, share 0.1, change fee 97.20 / 104.76 / 58.32 / 62.86 / 0); 33.00 / 32.25 / 36.89 / 36.44 / 42.72 (rate 0.9, share 0.1); 40.67 / 39.92 / 44.56 / 44.11 / 50.39 (rate 1, share 0.1); 61.36 / 69.02 / 76.69 (share 0). **The blind audit cannot settle a single value**: every candidate is definite once U1–U6 are known, and they differ.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root: paid Premium Economy upgrade on segment 2. Governing doc "Paid Upgrades into Premium Economy: Purchase Terms…", "When the charge is fixed":
- S1: "The Premium Economy upgrade charge is fixed only after the latest standard exchange recorded on the ticket carries its change fee entry, whenever that exchange owes a change fee."
- S2: "The Premium Economy upgrade charge on a segment is not fixed until every bag of that segment carrying a weight or size entry also carries its first, second or third bag charge."
- S3: "Before the Premium Economy upgrade charge on a segment is fixed, the heaviest bag charged by count on that segment must carry its weight or size entry whenever it owes a weight or size charge."

Hop 1 (S1) — **state-derived.** Record: exchange e8b3cd9b standard_change, no linked change fee entry. Words "change fee entry" / "standard exchange" reach "Change Fee Posting for Voluntary Exchanges" ("posted through the call center as one itinerary-level change fee entry linked to that exchange entry"; "A fee worked out at zero is not recorded"). Whether the state is already satisfied vacuously (fee zero) depends on U1 (a waiving tier → rate 0 → nothing owed). Otherwise owed.
Hop 2 (S2) — **state-derived.** Record: CR1047736 on segment 2 carries an overweight entry and no count charge. Words "first, second or third bag charge" / "weight or size entry" reach "Checked-Bag Charges by Place in the Bag Count: Ledger Posting Reference" ("governs the checked-bag charge owed for each bag … that carries a weight or size entry but no first, second or third bag charge").
Hop 3 (S3) — **state-derived.** Record: heaviest bag with a count charge on segment 2 is CR1047735 (72 lb), no weight/size entry. Words "heaviest bag charged by count" / "weight or size entry" reach "Weight and Size Charges on Checked Bags: Ledger Posting Reference" ("governs the weight-or-size charge owed for the heaviest bag carrying a first, second or third bag charge … when that bag carries no weight or size entry"). Owed because (C) = 66.88 > 0.
None of the three depended-on posting documents states a prerequisite of its own → depth 1, three leaves, mutually independent, all before pricing the upgrade. No hop pre-solved (the PE purchase doc names only its own tool).

Factor findability: agreement named on the ticket → the corporate factor docs (relief, brand rate, posting rate, points rate, corporate upgrade rate, trip-charge credit) all name "Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements" and the record kind (status, spend this agreement year, spend postings, points balance, booking channel); exchange date vs new departure → notice rates; bag charges' `sales_channel` airport → check-in channel rates and weight counting; weight entries standing → repeat rates; flown coupon date vs issue → booking lead rates; departure today → travel-day rates. Computation documents (change fee by origin, bag charge by place, weight-or-size list charge, PE upgrade price) contain no hint of modification.

### Two-way counter-proof

- Change-fee banding on 658.36 (→ 0.92) vs 540.00 (→ 0.96): the definition doc's first row ("Names an active corporate agreement | The fare collected less the ticket's taxes and fees") closes it. Note: "Change Fee Fare Bands" says only "measured from the fare collected on the ticket" — a reader who stops at that doc could band on 658.36; the definition doc is reachable by its exact defined term ("fare that bands the change fee").
- Change-fee base 0 (US-origin) vs 125: record `origin_region` outside_united_states; doc: "The origin region and itinerary class are those recorded on the ticket".
- Bag place 1 vs 2: "the number of first, second and third bag charges already recorded in the bag's direction plus one" (CR1047735 first_bag on the return).
- Bag channel online/call-center vs airport: "the airport when any bag charge of that segment was paid at the airport".
- Weight charge on 72 lb (second band 200 → rates) vs 69 lb (first band 100): weight-counting doc, airport row "recorded weight less the scale tolerance of 3 pounds".
- Weight charge on CR1047736 instead of CR1047735: it already carries a weight entry and is lighter.
- Booking lead from issue to next departure (22 days → 0.95) vs to flown segment-1 date (19 → 0.98): "the flight date recorded on the flown coupon of segment 1 when that coupon has been flown".
- **"Do only the upgrade"**: S1–S3 say the PE charge is not fixed until the three states hold; records show all three missing; each posting doc says the charge "is owed as soon as the records show …, whether or not the customer raises it". Doing only the upgrade leaves the governed result unfixed and changes the number (trip charges 135.00 instead of 263.01 + change fee).
- Fall-back answers: change fee 125.00; bag count charge 65.00; weight charge 200.00; PE upgrade 99.00 — all definite and different.

### Blind-phase finding carried forward (to be judged in gt_comparison)

The factor tiers U1–U6 rest on tier terms of Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements, which are not carried by any document visible at this audit (the ticket factor documents name the program and the record kinds, and no business-product corpus is published on disk). From the materials visible at audit time the upgrade price (and the change fee and possibly the bag charge) is **not uniquely derivable**. Whether this is a ticket-corpus defect or the expected pipelined absence of a sibling product is judged after the reveal; cross-product carriage is outside this skill's detection range by construction.

Also noted: both the bag tool schemas and the KB say `bag_tag_number` is "CR followed by 6 digits", while the records carry 7 digits (CR1047735, CR1047736); the tool accepted the 7-digit tag verbatim.

contamination_disclosure: none. No scored value was present in the brief; no recursive grep over the scenario tree; no source-layer file read.

Where the blind answer could not reach a unique value: only at U1–U5 (U6 happened to be inferable). Every one of them is a tier term of Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements, i.e. a parameter of the business charter. The ticket factor documents carry their ladders in full and name the program and the record kinds ("the change fee waiver and the annual spend threshold are those of the agreement's tier", "the negotiated discounts from its tier's terms, in Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements", "its tier's eligible booking channels are read from Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements", "the discount-eligible fare brands are the official fare brand names listed by the agreement's tier"). The figures belong to the business product's own corpus, which is not published (`docs/` has no `business/` directory at audit time). Under the single-homing contract this is not something the ticket corpus should carry, so it is not a ticket-corpus defect. It is also not proved absent: cross-product carriage is outside this skill's detection range, and at the moment a rollout would have no source for those six terms.

No difference arises on the ticket side: every ticket-side tier, convention, object, tool argument and ordering in the blind answer equals GT.

Other observations (not verdicts):
- Change-fee fare band document ("Change Fee Fare Bands"): "The fare that bands the change fee is measured from the fare collected on the ticket, which is every fare-collection and add-collect entry on its fare history." A reader who takes "measured from" as "equals" would band on 658.36 (0.92) and reach GT's method-factor baseline 55.89. The definition document ("Definition of the Fare That Bands the Change Fee") settles it explicitly for an active agreement (540.00 → 0.96), and it is reachable by the exact defined term. No visible sentence says the banding fare *equals* the fare collected, so this is a wording hazard, not a second formula. Detailed in the policy_kb file.
- Bag tag format: the tool schemas and KB say "CR followed by 6 digits", while the seeded tags have 7 digits (CR1047735, CR1047736). The KB follows the tool contract faithfully, and the gold argument is a verbatim copy (traceability gate green). This is a source-layer contract/seed inconsistency, noted for the policy side.

| "the change fee waiver … of the agreement's tier" (Corporate Agreement Relief on Change Fees) | "Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements Booking Channels, Tour Code and Ticket Allowances", column "Change fee waiver"; text: "The change fee waiver covers change fees and same-day change fees on tickets booked under the agreement" | no |

| "the discount-eligible fare brands are the official fare brand names listed by the agreement's tier" (Agreement Brand Rates on Change Fees) | "Negotiated Fare Discount Table…", column "Discount-eligible fare brands" | Crestline Main Cabin, Crestline Main Plus |

All six terms can be found using the ticket documents' own vocabulary, which is near-identical to the business column headers. Each is stated as a single tier figure, and the business corpus states no alternative figure anywhere (scoped scan for waiver, threshold, discount-eligible, negotiated discount, eligible booking channels and checked bags found no competing value).

### Resolving U1–U6 and the resulting derivation (not blind)

U1 no waiver; U2 spend 31,480.00 ≥ 25,000 → relief 0.6; U3 Main Cabin listed → brand rate 0.9; U4 domestic discount 3 (1–9) → corporate upgrade rate 0.9; U5 corporate booking tool listed, agreement active → credit share 0.1; U6 allowance 0 → bag place 2 is charged. With the unchanged ticket-side factors from revision_1, the candidate table of revision_1 collapses to one row. Change fee, bag count charge, weight charge and PE upgrade are exactly the revision_1 row that equals GT (the values are not repeated here). Tool sequence, owners, tree and hop marks: unchanged from revision_1, all state-derived.

### Cross-product observation (recorded, not a ticket-corpus verdict)

The business note "Fare Rules Note on Tickets Booked under Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements" says: "A ticket counts as booked under a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement only when … it is for a traveler on the agreement's active roster on the booking date", and "Tickets booked under the agreement also receive the change fee waiver and the corporate checked bag allowance". In this world `find_business_roster` returns "No roster entries found" for the agreement (by business_account_id and by customer_id). That is also below Business Connect Plus's stated minimum of 5 enrolled travelers. The ticket record names the agreement, and every ticket factor document keys its tier on "Agreement named on the ticket" / "Names an active agreement", read from the ticket's corporate agreement field and the agreement's status. None of them uses "booked under". Here the only benefits the business note gates on "booked under" are the change fee waiver (no for this tier) and the corporate bag allowance (0 = the brand allowance), so applying the roster test changes no number. A reader who instead extended the roster test to the ticket's own corporate rates (relief, brand, corporate upgrade, trip-charge credit, posting, points, banding convention) would depart from the explicit ticket wording. The visible ticket text closes that reading, so it is not a second equally reasonable formula. The seed oddity (an active agreement with an empty roster) and the "booked under" vs "named on the ticket" framing are passed to the business-corpus auditor and the policy side.
